# Four explanations, all of them wrong

The bill grew forty percent in a quarter. The first four theories were the new team, the ML workload, the vendor's
pricing, and general growth. All four were wrong, and the vendor's pricing had actually moved in our favor.

It was one dashboard. Refreshing every five minutes. Eleven people had it bookmarked and two of them opened it.

Finding it took an afternoon and one query grouped by warehouse, then by query hash. Thirty-one percent of the
increase sat on the top line. A test suite somebody had scheduled in 2024 and then left the company sat on the
second.

We moved the refresh to hourly and asked the two actual viewers whether that was a problem. Neither had noticed the
cadence existed.

The waste is not the part that bothers me. The bill had been climbing for two quarters and every meeting about it
had been a meeting about policy. Twelve people, six hours, zero queries.

So now there is a standing thirty-minute block the week after close. One person, one query, top ten consumers by
delta. It has found something every quarter and it has never once needed a policy to do it.

Run the query before you write the policy. The query takes an afternoon and it tells you what is actually true.
